mechanism_narrative: The current federal funds rate of 5.06% is above the long-term average of 4.5% but below the threshold of 5.5% that signals aggressive tightening, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS is within 0.1% of 5.06% (i.e., 5.06±0.1) over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL value above 3.5 (current value 303.294) signals persistent inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to anticipated monetary tightening.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL is above 3.5 over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 3.7% and employment falls below 156,105 thousand, it signals a deteriorating labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 3.7 and PAYEMS < 156105 over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: When quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) exceeds 20,000 billion (current value 20,246.439), it indicates robust economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when GDPC1 > 20000 over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate above 4.0% signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to immediate market reaction to labor market deterioration.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 4.0 over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 102 and the federal funds rate is at or above 5.06%, it signals a dual contraction in supply and aggressive monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 102 and FEDFUNDS >= 5.06 over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 100 (current value 103.01) signals a contraction in the industrial sector, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced economic activity.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100 over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 3.5%, it signals a tight labor market and strong economic conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE < 3.5 over the last 5 years.
